solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Are you, texting, grabbed by good-looking date?

indicators.note: being grabbed by something means being held within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: fit is British slang for attractive
in text-speak 'are you' is written as the two letters R and U

explanation.surface: Someone sends a flirty text asking whether a handsome date has caught them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'date' looks like a romantic evening, but it is the fruit of the date palm. 'Fit' is British slang for attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A date is an example of a sweet fruit from the date palm.

clue.text: Help! Turf her out!

definitions.note: as a verb, to help a cause is to advance or promote it

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A desperate cry to have some woman evicted from the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns TURFHER into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance or promote a cause is to help it along, a verb sense of the answer.

clue.text: Dishonest UN dignitary bears responsibility

indicators.note: to bear something is to carry it, so the first pieces hold the next one inside them

parts.note: a worthy is a notable or eminent person
a trust is a responsibility placed in someone's charge

explanation.surface: A United Nations official is answerable for something, though apparently a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' means carries within, so the dignitary from the UN holds the responsibility; 'worthy' as a noun is a notable person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not to be relied upon is dishonest; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Scotches? These could sink a battleship!

definitions.meaning: to scotch a plan is to wreck it, as torpedoing does figuratively
self-propelled underwater missiles fired at warships

explanation.surface: Whisky so strong it might sink a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotches' suggests whisky, but it is a verb meaning puts an end to.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpedoing a scheme means wrecking it, and the noun names underwater missiles that hole ships.

clue.text: At a loss, needing inspiration in bed

indicators.note: in places the inspiration within the bed

parts.note: taken as written
a muse is a source of creative inspiration

explanation.surface: A puzzled writer lying in bed waiting for an idea to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bewildered or puzzled is at a loss, a close synonym.

clue.text: Teacher with listening device — unwelcome companion between the sheets

parts.note: BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teaching degree
a bug is a hidden microphone

explanation.surface: A spying teacher turns out to be an unwanted bedfellow.
explanation.walkthrough: BEd is the Bachelor of Education degree held by many teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood-sucking insect that lives in mattresses is a decidedly unwanted bedfellow.

clue.text: Cleaner starts to merit outstanding pay

indicators.note: the starts of the following words give their opening letters

explanation.surface: A cleaner deserves to be paid what is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor-cleaning implement with a head of absorbent strands is a cleaner.

clue.text: President's IOU written off? That's fortunate

indicators.note: a written-off car is wrecked, so these letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A head of state's debt is cancelled, which is lucky for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written off' rearranges PRESIDENTSIOU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening by happy chance is fortunate; a near synonym.

clue.text: Shop I managed on the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: to lead is to manage, past tense led

explanation.surface: A shop someone ran during their rise to success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' reverses ILED.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a kind of shop selling cooked meats and cheeses.

clue.text: Socialist holding flag withdrew

indicators.note: holding means the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: red is a common label for a left-winger
to flag is to grow weary, to tire

explanation.surface: A left-wing protester with a banner pulls back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner, but it is a verb meaning grow tired.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat or pull back is to have withdrawn, the same past tense.

clue.text: Danger left one representative receding

indicators.note: receding means moving backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sales rep walks away from a risky situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receding' reverses LIREP.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is exposure to risk or harm, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Man staying at home with us: he had bonus slashed

indicators.note: slashed suggests cut up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stay-at-home dad lives with a family whose breadwinner had his bonus cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slashed' rearranges USHEHADBONUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A married man who keeps house while his wife earns is a domestic husband by description.

clue.text: Abused our benign Prime Minister once in Middle East

definitions.text: Prime Minister once in Middle East

indicators.note: abused means mistreated, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone mistreated a kindly former Middle Eastern leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abused' rearranges OURBENIGN. David Ben-Gurion was Israel's first Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: David Ben-Gurion founded Israel and was its first premier, a Middle Eastern head of government.

clue.text: Restrict speech with introduction missing

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A rule limiting speech, made without any preamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with introduction missing' drops the O at the front of ORATION.
explanation.definitionFit: To ration is to limit supply to fixed allowances, which restricts it.

clue.text: Swell the coffers of Henri Charrière to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Boosting the fortune of Henri Charrière, the convict who wrote Papillon.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in hENRI CHarrière.
explanation.definitionFit: To make wealthier is to fill someone's money chest; the definition is an idiom for it.

clue.text: Improve farm accommodation? It's the best policy

parts.note: to hone a skill is to sharpen or improve it
a sty is a pig's pen on a farm

explanation.surface: Upgrading the pig pens is the wisest choice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'honesty is the best policy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says truthfulness is the best policy, so the definition stands for it.

clue.text: Trendy WAG attacked

parts.note: a wag is a joker, a wit
to hit someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A fashionable footballer's wife or girlfriend was assaulted.
explanation.walkthrough: WAG in capitals suggests the British tabloid term for footballers' wives and girlfriends, but here it is a joker.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fashionable and up to date is the 1960s slang sense of being trendy.

clue.text: Health organisation

definitions.meaning: a person's physical make-up and state of wellbeing
the composition or structure of something, or a body of founding rules

explanation.surface: A health body, read as a two-word heading.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person's physical health and the way something is made up or organised.

clue.text: Edge inside bunker, briefly

indicators.note: inside says the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A golfer edges briefly into a bunker.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in bunKER Briefly; 'briefly' looks like it shortens bunker but just supplies the B.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised stone border of a pavement is its edge; British spelling of curb.

clue.text: Polished off school broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put out on air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school's television broadcast is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is England's best-known private boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been polished off has been consumed entirely.

clue.text: Sister having nothing to say

indicators.note: to say signals the word is spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: none means not any, nothing

explanation.surface: A sibling who stays silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having nothing to say' reads as being quiet, but 'to say' marks a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is addressed as Sister in a religious order.

clue.text: Ambassador beginning to ignore common sense? Disgraceful

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: the beginning of the word gives its first letter

parts.note: nous is British slang for practical good sense

explanation.surface: An envoy starting to disregard common sense is shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title; nous is British informal for common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked or shockingly evil conduct is disgraceful, a strong synonym.

clue.text: Spike, neat boy when dressed up

indicators.note: dressing up changes appearance, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tidy lad in costume carries a spike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when dressed up' rearranges NEATBOY.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade fixed to a rifle muzzle is a type of spike.

clue.text: Mean and ill-considered, taking note instead initially

indicators.note: instead at the start says the opening letter is swapped for another

parts.note: hasty means rash or ill-considered

explanation.surface: A spiteful and rash remark noted at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instead initially' swaps the H at the start of HASTY for N.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkind or spiteful behaviour is mean, the adjective sense.
